parsed.rationale: This is not a normal ECG: the QRS is wide (about 140 ms or more), V1–V3 show deep QS/rS complexes, I, aVL, V5 and V6 have broad notched R waves with no septal q waves, and the ST/T changes run opposite to the QRS, so this is a typical LBBB with left axis deviation, and the ST elevation in V1–V3 is proportionate to the deep S waves (ST/S ratio below 0.25, no concordant changes), so it does not meet Sgarbossa or STEMI criteria.
